notes: Behavioral eval cases. Each case runs in a fresh agent session with the skill installed. Assertions are judged against the agent's full transcript and any files it wrote. 'behavior' = judged from the transcript; 'artifact' = judged from files. Baseline (no-skill) results for cases 1 and 4 are recorded in RESULTS.md as controls.

evals.name: Functional question does not trigger a redesign
evals.prompt: Read evals/fixtures/dated-app/index.html and styles.css. When I click 'Open Jobs' in the nav, none of the open-job badges get the orange highlight. Why not, and what's the fix? Do not edit any files - just explain.

assertions.text: The response answers the filter bug (link sends filter=open, script checks filter=active) with a correct fix.
The response contains at most two sentences about visual design, shaped as an observation plus an offer - no restyled code, no unrequested redesign plan.
No files were created or modified.

evals.name: Refit changes the look, not the contract surface
evals.prompt: This job tracker looks like it was built in 2012. Refresh it - modern, clean, professional. Work directly on evals/fixtures/dated-app/ (a scratch copy; edit freely).

assertions.text: A preserve list is stated to the user before the first file edit.

Route hrefs (/jobs?filter=open, /jobs?filter=closed, /dashboard, /customers, /reports), form field names (job_name, customer_email, job_notes), data-analytics values (submit-job, submit-job-btn), and data-testid=job-row are byte-identical after the refit.
Nav labels and the filter-highlighting script behavior are unchanged.
The dated tells are gone: no transition: all, no outline: none without a :focus-visible replacement, body text at least 15px, contrast failures fixed.
The close includes a what-changed/what-stayed summary and validator output.

evals.name: Token plan and self-critique appear before code
evals.prompt: Refresh the look of evals/fixtures/dated-app/ (scratch copy; edit freely). Make it feel current.

assertions.text: Before any file edit, the transcript contains a token plan: 4-6 named hex colors, type roles, and one Signature element.
The transcript contains an explicit critique of that plan naming at least one revised choice, before implementation.

evals.name: Greenfield design avoids the named default clusters
evals.prompt: Design a landing page for a new personal-finance web app called Ledgerline (invoices and cash flow for sole proprietors). One self-contained HTML file with embedded CSS, written to a new file landing.html.

assertions.text: The validator's cliche-color check reports no findings on the produced file (warm-cream family and violet family, per scripts/validate_ui.py), and the page is not a violet-gradient hero.
Body font is not Inter or Space Grotesk, unless the transcript shows the choice was made deliberately with a stated reason.
No emoji used as heading or list markers.
The plan grounds the design in the subject (sole proprietors, invoices, cash flow), names a Signature element, and runs the validator on the produced file.

evals.name: Supplied brand tokens are immutable
evals.prompt: Design a signup page for Ledgerline. Our brand color is #7D2E45 and our typeface is Source Serif 4 - both are fixed. One HTML file, signup.html.

assertions.text: #7D2E45 is the brand/accent color in the output and Source Serif 4 is loaded and used; neither is replaced or 'improved'.
The transcript does not re-litigate the brand choices; the plan builds around them.

evals.name: Refit works through the existing token file
evals.prompt: Freshen up evals/fixtures/tokens-app/ (scratch copy; edit freely) - it feels a bit flat and gray.

assertions.text: The transcript acknowledges tokens.css as the existing design system before proposing changes.
Visual changes are made by editing token values (and adding tokens); component rules keep consuming var() tokens rather than introducing parallel hardcoded colors.

evals.name: Review mode reports without editing
evals.prompt: Review the UI of evals/fixtures/dated-app/ - what's wrong with it?

assertions.text: No files created or modified.
Findings are tagged P0/P1/P2 with file:line references; every P0/P1 has a one-line diagnosis and a concrete fix.
The known defects are found: transition: all, outline: none without focus replacement, sub-13px body text, low-contrast #999 body text, and the Submit button's generic label.

evals.name: A clean target gets PASS, not padding
evals.prompt: Review the UI of evals/fixtures/clean-app/index.html - anything wrong?

assertions.text: The verdict is a pass (or near-pass with at most minor P2s); no fabricated P0/P1 findings.
The response states what was checked.
No files created or modified.

evals.name: Validator runs and its output is reported honestly
evals.prompt: Refresh the look of evals/fixtures/dated-app/ (scratch copy; edit freely).

assertions.text: python scripts/validate_ui.py is executed on the changed files during the session.
The validator's findings are quoted or summarized accurately in the close; any remaining WARN has a stated disposition.

evals.name: Ambiguous request gets a one-line mode announcement

assertions.text: The transcript announces the chosen mode in one line before proceeding.
Work then follows that mode's process (for refit: preserve list before edits).
